newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish '96 broad money growth not inflationary-NBP.
newsitem.headline: Polish '96 broad money growth not inflationary-NBP.

text.p: Last year's 29.0 percent growth in Polish broad money supply did not stimulate price growth, which in December was 18.5 percent in year-on-year terms, deputy central bank president Witold Kozinski said.
"Broad money growth in 1996 was not inflationary," Kozinski told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.
The most inflationary element of money supply, cash in circulation, increased by 20.6 percent in 1996, while the average rate of inflation for the whole year was 19.9 percent. @
Kozinski said the changes in bank account regulations from January 1 artificially inflated money supply growth in December, to month-on-month 5.1 percent.
Kozinski said that were it not for December's larger-than- planned increase, broad money growth in all of 1996 would match central bank's initial forecasts at between 24.2-28.5 percent.
